stem: A company with one Microsoft Entra tenant is designing its Log Analytics architecture and wants as few workspaces as possible. Which two requirements justify creating an additional workspace? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Logs from resources in the EU must be stored only in an EU region, while US resources may log to a US region
Total ingestion is expected to reach several terabytes, which would slow down queries in a single workspace
Each application team wants its own dashboards and should see only the logs of the resources it manages
Security analysts need to correlate sign-in data, firewall logs and VM events from every team in one query
The same table must keep data from production resources for two years but data from test resources for 30 days

stem: A security team will run Microsoft Sentinel and wants sole ownership of its data. The operations team ingests large volumes of performance and application logs that never need security analytics. Cost must be minimized. Which workspace design should you recommend?

choices.text: A separate workspace per resource group, each with Microsoft Sentinel enabled so that both teams see the same tools
One combined workspace with Microsoft Sentinel enabled, and resource-context access for every operations team member
One combined workspace with Microsoft Sentinel enabled, and table-level RBAC that hides the security tables from operators
A dedicated workspace for Microsoft Sentinel and a separate workspace without Sentinel for the operational data

stem: Eight business units each keep their own Log Analytics workspace in West Europe; together they ingest about 300 GB per day. Compliance requires customer-managed encryption keys. How should you meet this and lower ingestion cost?

choices.text: Set a commitment tier on each of the eight workspaces and configure a customer-managed key on each workspace directly
Create a Log Analytics dedicated cluster in West Europe with a commitment tier and link all eight workspaces to it
Merge the eight workspaces into one workspace and give each unit resource-context access to its own resources' data
Add all eight workspaces to one Azure Monitor Private Link Scope so that their data is encrypted with a private key

stem: A central workspace receives logs from all subscriptions. App teams have Reader on their own resource groups and must query only their resources' logs, without being granted any workspace permissions. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Configure table-level RBAC that grants each team read access only to the tables that its own resources write data into
Set the access control mode to Require workspace permissions and grant each team Log Analytics Reader on the workspace
Keep the access control mode Use resource or workspace permissions and let teams query logs from their resources (resource-context)
Create one workspace per team and redirect each resource's diagnostic settings to the workspace of the team that owns it

stem: A managed service provider monitors Azure resources, including PaaS services, for 40 customers, each in its own Microsoft Entra tenant. Customers require isolated data, their own retention and billing. Admins must not sign in to each tenant. What should you recommend?

choices.text: One workspace in the provider's tenant that collects every customer's logs, with each customer separated by subscription ID in queries
A workspace in each customer tenant, with provider admins given delegated access to all of them through Azure Lighthouse onboarding
A workspace in each customer tenant, with each provider admin invited as a Microsoft Entra B2B guest user into every customer tenant
A workspace in each customer tenant, with a scheduled Logic App that copies all customer data into a single provider workspace daily

stem: Resource logs from regional Azure resources must reach a non-Microsoft SIEM in near real time and also be archived for seven years at low cost so that no one can alter them. Which two destinations should the diagnostic settings use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An Event Hubs namespace in the same region as the monitored resources, read by the SIEM's connector
An Event Grid custom topic in the same region that forwards each log record to the SIEM's endpoint
A Standard storage account in the same region with a time-based immutability policy on the container
A Premium block blob storage account with a legal hold placed on the container that stores the logs
A Log Analytics workspace with a seven-year total retention that the SIEM queries through the API

stem: Auditors need to know who created or deleted resources in a subscription over the past three years, queried with KQL together with other operational logs. Today only the portal's activity log is used. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Increase the activity log retention period of the subscription to three years from the subscription's activity log settings
Use Azure Resource Graph queries, because Resource Graph stores every create and delete operation for the lifetime of a subscription
Export the activity log to CSV from the portal every month and upload the files to a storage account that auditors can query with KQL
Create a diagnostic setting for the subscription activity log that sends it to a Log Analytics workspace with three-year table retention

stem: A company has 250 Windows VMs in Azure and 150 Windows servers on-premises. It needs the same Windows event IDs and performance counters from all of them, managed from one central definition. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Arc-enable the on-premises servers, install Azure Monitor Agent on all 400 machines and associate one data collection rule with them
Enable a diagnostic setting on each Azure VM resource, and use the same diagnostic setting on the on-premises servers through VPN
Write a scheduled script on each server that reads the events and posts them to the workspace through the Logs Ingestion API
Install the legacy Log Analytics agent on all servers and configure event and counter collection in each workspace's agent settings

stem: Azure Monitor Agent collects a custom application text log into a Log Analytics table. One column contains customer account numbers that must never be stored in the workspace. Other columns must still be collected. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Move the custom table to the Basic table plan so that the account number column is kept out of interactive query results
Create a data export rule for the table with a filter that drops the account number column before data is sent to storage
Add an ingestion-time transformation to the data collection rule that removes the account number column before storage
Grant table-level RBAC on the custom table so that only the security team can read the column with account numbers in it

stem: A custom app sends very verbose debug logs to a DCR-based custom table, tens of GB per day. Engineers query them only during incident investigations within 30 days, and no alerts use them. How should you minimize cost?

choices.text: Stop sending the logs to Log Analytics and write them only to blob storage that engineers download and search by hand
Set the table to the Basic plan, which lowers ingestion cost and still supports KQL queries during investigations
Keep the Analytics plan on the table and lower its analytics retention to four days so that much less data is billed
Move the table to a new workspace that uses the highest commitment tier so that each GB of debug logs costs less

stem: A compliance policy requires sign-in audit data to be interactively queryable for 180 days and kept for seven years in total. The data must stay in Log Analytics without a separate export pipeline. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Set the table's analytics retention to seven years so that every record stays available for interactive queries for the whole period
Keep the default workspace retention and rely on Azure Backup for Log Analytics to restore older records into the workspace
Set the table to the Basic plan with seven-year total retention so that all seven years stay interactively queryable at lower cost
Set analytics retention to 180 days and total retention to seven years, and use search jobs for records older than 180 days

stem: Azure Monitor Agent sends Windows event logs from hundreds of VMs to the Event table of a workspace. A downstream analytics platform must receive every new Event record continuously as it arrives. What should you recommend?

choices.text: A Log Analytics data export rule for the Event table with an event hub destination in the workspace's region
A summary rule in the workspace that aggregates the Event table every hour and writes the results to an event hub topic
A diagnostic setting on the Log Analytics workspace that streams the workspace's logs to an event hub in the same region
A Logic App that runs a log query every five minutes and posts the returned Event rows to the analytics platform

stem: An on-premises application must send custom JSON logs to a Log Analytics workspace that is reachable only through an Azure Monitor Private Link Scope. Records must be reshaped before storage. Which ingestion method should you recommend?

choices.text: An Application Insights availability test that posts the JSON records to the workspace every minute
The HTTP Data Collector API, signing each request with the workspace's shared key and the workspace ID
The Logs Ingestion API with a data collection rule that defines the schema, transformation and table
A diagnostic setting created for the on-premises application that targets the workspace in the scope

stem: All VMs in three Azure regions send guest performance counters to one workspace. Operations wants a single alert rule that fires a separate alert for each VM whose free disk space drops below 10%. What should you recommend?

choices.text: One activity log alert rule scoped to the subscriptions that fires when a VM writes a low disk space event
One log search alert rule on the workspace that queries the counter and splits by the resource ID column
One Resource Health alert rule that fires when any VM in the subscriptions reports a degraded disk state
One metric alert rule with all VMs as its scope, using a static threshold on the platform metric for free disk space

stem: Every Saturday from 01:00 to 05:00, a subscription's VMs are patched. Alerts must still be recorded during the window, but no one should be emailed or paged. You need the simplest solution to maintain. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Change every metric alert rule to stateless so that each alert fires once and then stays silent until 05:00
An Azure Automation runbook that disables every alert rule at 01:00 and re-enables all the rules again at 05:00
Remove the action groups from every alert rule and ask on-call staff to check the Alerts page for new alerts
An alert processing rule scoped to the subscription that suppresses action groups on a recurring weekly schedule

stem: Operations wants an email and an ITSM ticket whenever Microsoft reports an outage, planned maintenance or a health advisory for the Azure services and regions the company uses. What should you recommend?

choices.text: A metric alert on the Availability metric of each resource that fires when the value drops below 100 percent
A Service Health alert scoped to the company's subscriptions, services and regions, with an action group
A subscription to the public Azure status page feed, forwarded to the ITSM tool by a scheduled Logic App
A Resource Health alert on each critical resource that fires when that resource changes to the Unavailable state

stem: A web front end on App Service calls six microservices on AKS. Developers need end-to-end transaction tracing, an application map and failure analysis, using vendor-neutral instrumentation. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Workspace-based Application Insights, with the apps instrumented by the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro
VM insights on the AKS node pools, with the dependency map enabled to show calls between services
Network Watcher connection monitor tests between the front end and each microservice's endpoint
Container insights on the AKS cluster, with App Service diagnostic logs sent to the same workspace

stem: A public website must be checked from several geographic locations every few minutes, with alerts if it stops responding or its TLS certificate is close to expiring. The solution must use a currently recommended feature. What should you recommend?

choices.text: A Network Watcher connection monitor test with an HTTP configuration from VMs in two regions
A Resource Health alert on the App Service app that fires when the app becomes Unavailable
An Application Insights Standard test with SSL certificate validity and proactive lifetime check
An Application Insights URL ping test against the home page, with alerts on failed locations

stem: A workspace ingests about 20 GB per day, mainly from diagnostic settings that use the allLogs category group and from AMA. Much of it is never queried. Which two changes should you recommend to reduce ingestion cost? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable Microsoft Sentinel on the workspace to get three months of retention without extra charge
Add AllMetrics to every diagnostic setting so that metrics replace the logs that are not needed
Reduce the default analytics retention of the workspace to seven days for all Analytics tables
Change the diagnostic settings to collect only the log categories each service actually needs
Add transformations that drop rows nobody uses before they are written to the workspace's tables

stem: The network team must record all IP flows in several virtual networks, see which network rules allowed or denied each flow, and view traffic patterns on maps and dashboards. What should you recommend for new deployments?

choices.text: Network Watcher packet capture sessions on every VM, saved to a storage account and queried with KQL
Virtual network flow logs on each virtual network, with traffic analytics in a Log Analytics workspace
NSG flow logs on every network security group, with traffic analytics sending the results to Log Analytics
Connection monitor tests between all subnets, with results stored in a workspace for traffic dashboards

stem: A hybrid app runs on Azure VMs and on Arc-enabled on-premises servers. The network team needs ongoing measurement of latency and packet loss between both sites, with alerts when they degrade. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Network Watcher connection monitor, with Azure VMs and Arc-enabled servers as sources in test groups
Network Watcher connection troubleshoot, run from an Azure VM against each on-premises server's IP address
Network Watcher IP flow verify between each Azure VM and the on-premises address of the application
Network Watcher VPN troubleshoot on the virtual network gateway that connects the two sites together

stem: Traffic from an Azure VM to an on-premises subnet should pass through an Azure Firewall in the hub, but connections fail. You must find out whether the route sends traffic to the firewall and whether an NSG blocks it. Which two Network Watcher tools should you use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Topology, to draw the hub and spoke network and show which subnets the firewall is deployed into
Traffic analytics, to show maps of the busiest flows between the virtual networks over the last day
IP flow verify, to see whether the NSG rules allow the packet and which rule allows or denies it
Packet capture on the firewall, to record the full packets that the firewall sends to the on-premises network
Next hop, to see the next hop type and IP address the VM's route takes to the on-premises address

stem: VNets and on-premises networks (over ExpressRoute private peering) share one DNS. Monitoring traffic must use only private connectivity, and clients must not be able to send data to workspaces outside the company's approved list. What should you recommend?

choices.text: One Azure Monitor Private Link Scope per virtual network with a private endpoint, each configured to use the Open access mode
A private endpoint for each Log Analytics workspace, each in its own private DNS zone, with public network access left enabled
A service endpoint for Azure Monitor on every subnet, with the workspaces' firewalls allowing only those subnets to connect
One Azure Monitor Private Link Scope with the approved resources and a private endpoint, using Private Only access mode

stem: A retailer is designing a shopping cart service on Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL with one write region and two read regions. Each shopper must always see the items they just added to their own cart, while read latency, availability and RU cost should stay as close as possible to the weakest consistency level. Which default consistency level should you recommend?

choices.text: Strong consistency, which makes every read return the latest committed write in all regions
Eventual consistency, which serves each read from any single replica in the local region
Bounded staleness, which keeps every read region within a configured lag of K versions or T time
Session consistency, which gives each client session read-your-writes using its session token

stem: A market data service uses Azure Cosmos DB with a single write region in West Europe and read regions on three other continents. Readers in every region must never be more than 10 minutes behind the writer and must see updates in order, but write latency must not depend on cross-continent round trips. Which consistency level should you recommend?

choices.text: Bounded staleness, with the time bound set so that read regions lag the write region by 10 minutes at most
Session, so that each reader session receives a token that limits how stale its reads can become
Eventual, combined with a monitoring alert on the Probabilistically Bounded Staleness metric for each region
Strong, so that every read region always returns the most recent committed version of each item

stem: An Azure Cosmos DB account with one write region and one read region uses session consistency. The architects propose switching the default consistency to strong. Which two effects should you expect from this change? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The account can then enable multiple write regions to lower the write latency added by strong mode
Write latency increases, because each write must commit in both regions before it is acknowledged
Reads in the read region can return items that are up to K versions older than the write region
The RU charge for reads is halved, because strong reads come from a single replica with no token
Each read consumes about twice as many request units, because reads are served from two replicas

stem: An online store will keep orders for about 50,000 customers in an Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL container. Most queries read all orders of one customer, and writes surge during flash sales. Which partition key should you recommend?

choices.text: /id, so that every order gets its own logical partition and writes spread as evenly as possible
/orderStatus, so that open, shipped and returned orders are each grouped into their own partition
/customerId, so that one customer's orders share a partition and writes spread across many values
/orderDate, so that each day's orders form one logical partition that is easy to archive later

stem: A SaaS provider stores events for all tenants in one Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL container partitioned by /tenantId. A few large tenants are approaching the 20 GB logical partition limit, and most queries filter on a single tenant. What should you recommend for a new container?

choices.text: Hierarchical partition keys of /tenantId then /userId, so that one tenant's data can span partitions
A partition key of /userId, so that each user's events form their own small logical partition
A synthetic partition key that appends a random suffix from 1 to 10 to each tenantId value
The same /tenantId key with a much higher autoscale maximum, which raises the logical partition size limit

stem: A team is building a proof-of-concept app on Azure Cosmos DB in one region. Traffic is idle most of the week with short, unpredictable bursts, and the team wants to pay only for the database operations that actually run. Which capacity option should you recommend?

choices.text: Provisioned throughput shared at the database level, so that idle containers lend their RU/s to busy containers
Standard (manual) provisioned throughput set to the expected peak, reduced by a scheduled job outside office hours
Serverless capacity mode, which bills for the request units consumed with no throughput provisioned in advance
Autoscale provisioned throughput with a low maximum, so throughput drops to a fraction of the maximum between bursts

stem: A company runs a self-managed Apache Cassandra cluster for device telemetry. It wants a fully managed Azure service with global distribution, without sizing or patching nodes, and it must keep its existing CQL drivers and queries with minimal code changes. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Azure Table Storage, with each Cassandra table mapped to a table keyed by PartitionKey and RowKey
Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Cassandra, which supports the Cassandra Query Language and existing drivers
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, with the application rewritten to use the NoSQL SDK and SQL queries
Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, with the wide-column tables converted to relational schemas

stem: An IoT platform writes device readings to an Azure Cosmos DB container. Readings are only needed for 30 days, and the design must remove older items automatically without writing or scheduling any cleanup code. What should you recommend?

choices.text: A change feed processor in Azure Functions that deletes each item 30 days after it was written
Setting the container's default time to live to -1, so that every item expires on its own schedule
An Azure Storage lifecycle management policy that deletes items when they are older than 30 days
Setting the container's default time to live to 2,592,000 seconds, so items expire 30 days after their last change

stem: A hospital must keep scanned records in Azure Blob Storage for 10 years. Each record is opened perhaps once a year, but when a doctor requests one it must open within seconds. Which access tier should you recommend to minimize cost?

choices.text: Cold tier, an online tier with lower storage cost than cool and immediate reads
Archive tier, with standard-priority rehydration when a doctor requests a record
Hot tier, with reserved capacity purchased to lower the storage price per gigabyte
Cool tier, an online tier for data kept at least 30 days and read occasionally

stem: A company keeps documents in a ZRS general-purpose v2 storage account. A new lifecycle rule should move audit files older than one year to the archive tier, but the blobs never change tier. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Upgrade the account to a premium block blob account, because the archive tier requires SSD-backed storage
Store the audit files in a separate LRS or GRS account, because the archive tier is not supported with ZRS
Change the account's default access tier to archive, so that existing audit files inherit the archive tier
Enable blob versioning on the account, because lifecycle actions to archive apply only to blob versions

stem: A legal team needs a 4 GB contract that was moved to the archive tier last year. The file must be readable in under an hour, and extra cost is acceptable. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Generate a SAS for the archived blob, so that the legal team can download it directly from the archive tier
Rehydrate the blob to the hot tier with standard priority, which completes within one hour for blobs under 10 GB
Rehydrate the blob to an online tier with high priority, which can complete in under an hour for blobs under 10 GB
Change the account's default access tier to hot, so that the archived blob is moved back online automatically

stem: A media company wants blobs moved from hot to cool automatically when nobody has read them for 60 days, even if they were created years ago, and wants this done without custom code. Which two actions should you recommend? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add a lifecycle rule that moves blobs to cool when daysAfterModificationGreaterThan is 60
Change the account's default access tier to cool, so that unread blobs move after 60 days
Enable blob versioning, so that lifecycle rules can see each blob's read history
Enable last access time tracking on the storage account
Add a lifecycle rule that moves blobs to cool when daysAfterLastAccessTimeGreaterThan is 60

stem: A broker-dealer must keep trade confirmations in Azure Blob Storage for seven years in a state that no user, including account administrators, can modify or delete, and the setup must satisfy SEC Rule 17a-4(f). What should you recommend?

choices.text: A CanNotDelete resource lock on the storage account, combined with soft delete for seven years
A legal hold on the container, combined with a lifecycle rule that deletes blobs after seven years
A time-based retention policy of seven years on the container, kept unlocked so it can be adjusted
A time-based retention policy of seven years on the container, locked after testing is complete

stem: A data platform team will store petabytes of files for Apache Spark jobs. They need directory and file level permissions for Microsoft Entra groups, and renaming a directory with millions of files must be a single fast operation. What should you recommend?

choices.text: An Azure Files SMB share with NTFS permissions, mounted on every Spark worker node to read and write data files
A general-purpose v2 account with the hierarchical namespace enabled for Data Lake Storage, secured with POSIX-like ACLs
A premium block blob account with a flat namespace, secured with user delegation SAS tokens scoped to each folder prefix
A general-purpose v2 account with containers and blob index tags that emulate folders, secured with container-level Azure RBAC

stem: A government agency stores case files in Azure Storage. Data governance rules forbid any copy outside the chosen region, and the data must survive the loss of an entire datacenter without data loss. Which redundancy option should you recommend at the lowest cost?

choices.text: Geo-zone-redundant storage (GZRS), which combines zone copies with a secondary region copy
Geo-redundant storage (GRS), which copies data asynchronously to a paired secondary region
Zone-redundant storage (ZRS), which copies data synchronously across availability zones
Locally redundant storage (LRS), which keeps three copies inside a single datacenter

stem: An engineering firm will move a Linux and Windows simulation workload to Azure. Both platforms must access the same volume over NFSv3 and SMB at the same time, with submillisecond latency. Which storage service should you recommend?

choices.text: Azure NetApp Files with a dual-protocol volume in a Premium or Ultra service level
Azure Blob Storage with NFS 3.0 enabled, plus an Azure file share kept in sync for Windows
Azure Files HDD share over SMB, cached on each simulation node with Azure File Sync
Azure Files SSD file share with the NFS 4.1 protocol, accessed by Linux and Windows clients

stem: A company has 30 branch offices, each with a Windows Server file server whose disks are nearly full. It wants a central copy of all files in Azure, fast local access to frequently used files, and older files to stop consuming local disk. What should you recommend?

choices.text: A nightly AzCopy job on each branch server that copies changed files to a container in Blob Storage
Azure File Sync with Azure file shares as cloud endpoints and cloud tiering enabled on each branch server
Azure file shares mounted directly by branch users over SMB, through a private endpoint reached by VPN
Azure NetApp Files volumes in the nearest region, mounted by branch users over the VPN connection

stem: Linux application servers in an Azure virtual network need a shared POSIX file system, and the team selected Azure Files with the NFS protocol. Which two design decisions are required? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Deploy Azure File Sync on the Linux servers, so that each server keeps a local cached copy of the share
Create the share on HDD (standard) media to lower cost, because NFS shares are offered on both media tiers
Enable Microsoft Entra Kerberos on the share, so that each Linux user authenticates with their own identity
Create the share on SSD (premium) media, because NFS Azure file shares are offered only on SSD
Restrict access to the share through a private endpoint or service endpoint in the virtual network

stem: A manufacturer must copy data every night from an on-premises SQL Server to Azure Data Lake Storage. The corporate firewall allows outbound HTTPS only and no inbound connections. Which integration design should you recommend?

choices.text: Azure Data Factory with a self-hosted integration runtime installed on a server inside the corporate network
Azure Event Hubs Capture, with SQL Server sending each changed row to an event hub through a custom trigger
Azure Data Factory with an Azure-SSIS integration runtime that runs a new SSIS package to copy the tables
Azure Data Factory with an Azure integration runtime that connects to the SQL Server through a public IP address

stem: A company has about 200 SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS) packages and wants to run them in Azure with minimal rework and without managing virtual machines. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Run each package as a Stream Analytics job reading from and writing to the same data sources
Rebuild each package as a mapping data flow in Azure Data Factory and schedule them with triggers
Provision an Azure-SSIS integration runtime in Azure Data Factory, with SSISDB hosted in Azure SQL Database
Convert each package into a notebook in Azure Databricks and orchestrate them with Databricks jobs

stem: Data engineers who do not write Spark code must join, aggregate and cleanse large datasets inside Azure Data Factory pipelines, with the work scaled out automatically. Which pipeline component should you recommend?

choices.text: A stored procedure activity, which runs T-SQL in Azure SQL Database after the raw data is loaded there
A Databricks notebook activity, which runs PySpark code written by the team on an attached cluster
A copy activity with column mapping, which renames and converts columns while data moves to the sink
A mapping data flow, which is designed visually and runs on managed, scaled-out Apache Spark clusters

stem: A Data Factory pipeline processes sales data in hourly slices. The design must also process every hourly slice of the past six months, retry failed slices automatically, and pass each slice's start and end time to the pipeline. Which trigger type should you recommend?

choices.text: A storage event trigger that runs the pipeline whenever a new sales file arrives in the container
A schedule trigger with an hourly recurrence and a start time set six months in the past
A tumbling window trigger with a one-hour window and a start date six months in the past
A custom event trigger that runs the pipeline for each hourly event published to Event Grid

stem: Sensors send readings through Azure IoT Hub. The company needs the average temperature per device for each non-overlapping 5-minute period in near real time, using SQL-like queries and no clusters to manage. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Event Hubs Capture to Data Lake Storage, with a Synapse serverless SQL query run every 5 minutes
An Azure Stream Analytics job that groups readings by device and TumblingWindow(minute, 5)
An Azure Stream Analytics job that groups readings by device and HoppingWindow(minute, 5, 1)
An Azure Data Factory pipeline on a 5-minute schedule trigger that queries the IoT Hub messages

stem: An app sends clickstream events to an Azure Event Hubs namespace in the Basic tier. The data team now needs every raw event stored in Azure Data Lake Storage for later batch processing, without writing or hosting any consumer code. Which two actions should you recommend? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Upgrade the Event Hubs namespace to the Standard tier or higher, because the Basic tier doesn't support Capture
Write an Azure Functions consumer that reads each partition and appends the events to files in the data lake
Increase the event hub's retention period to its maximum, so that the events remain available for batch reads
Use a premium block blob storage account as the Capture destination, so that captured files are written faster
Enable Event Hubs Capture on the event hub with a Data Lake Storage account as the destination

stem: Analysts occasionally run ad hoc T-SQL queries over Parquet and CSV files in Azure Data Lake Storage. The company does not want to load the files into a database or pay for reserved compute between queries. What should you recommend?

choices.text: An Azure Synapse serverless SQL pool that queries the files in place and bills per data processed
An Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool that loads the files into distributed tables each night
An Azure SQL Database in the serverless tier that imports the files on demand when queried
An Azure Data Explorer cluster that ingests the files into tables for fast ad hoc exploration

stem: A data science team wants a collaborative platform for Python and Scala notebooks on Apache Spark, storing curated data as Delta Lake tables in the data lake and tracking machine learning experiments with MLflow. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Azure Data Factory mapping data flows that write curated data to Delta Lake tables in the data lake
Azure Databricks workspaces with clusters for notebooks, Delta Lake tables and MLflow tracking
Azure Synapse serverless SQL pool views over the data lake, queried from Python notebooks
Azure Stream Analytics jobs that write curated data to Data Lake Storage as Parquet files

stem: Analysts in Microsoft Fabric need near-real-time reports over an Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL container without consuming its request units, and must also use existing Delta tables in an Azure Data Lake Storage account without copying them. Which two features should you recommend? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB, which exposes the container's analytical store to Synapse
A Data Factory copy pipeline that reads the Cosmos DB container every 15 minutes into a lakehouse
A OneLake shortcut in a lakehouse that points to the Delta tables in the Data Lake Storage account
A Fabric pipeline that copies the Delta tables from Data Lake Storage into the lakehouse Tables folder
Mirroring in Fabric for the Azure Cosmos DB database, which replicates its data into OneLake

stem: Security policy disables public network access on the storage accounts and Azure SQL databases that Azure Data Factory copies between. The team must not run or patch any integration runtime VMs and wants protection against data exfiltration. What should you recommend?

choices.text: An Azure integration runtime without a managed network, with its regional IP ranges added to each store's firewall
A self-hosted integration runtime on Azure VMs in a spoke virtual network that has private endpoints to the stores
An Azure-SSIS integration runtime joined to a virtual network, running the copy logic as SSIS packages
An Azure integration runtime in a managed virtual network, with managed private endpoints to each data store
